title: Maple Leafs’ Auston Matthews out for 2025-26 season after knee-on-knee hit
content:
Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews will miss the remainder of the regular season with a knee injury, the team announced Friday.

“Matthews sustained a Grade 3 MCL tear and quad contusion on March 12 during the second period of the team’s game against the Anaheim Ducks,” the statement said.

“Matthews will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks. A further update will be provided at that time. He will miss the remainder of the 2025-26 season.”

Matthews sustained the injury after a nasty knee-on-knee collision with Anaheim Ducks defenseman Radko Gudas during the second period of Thursday’s 6-4 win. Gudas was immediately ejected from the game and had a phone hearing scheduled with the NHL’s Department of Player Safety on Friday afternoon.

Matthews required assistance to leave the ice after the hit.

“That’s a dirty play,” Leafs head coach Craig Berube said after the game Thursday.

The injury is another blow to the Leafs in a deflating season that will likely see them miss the playoffs for the first time since 2017. The Leafs’ win over the Ducks saw them snap an eight-game winless streak.

“I feel I’m just going to continue to repeat myself here, but it’s tough. We’re in a stretch where everything that seems to possibly go wrong, goes wrong,” Matthews said of the Leafs’ woes on March 9, his final media availability of the season.

Matthews’ knee injury comes after recent struggles with different injuries.

He sustained what the Leafs called a lower-body injury in November during a game against the Boston Bruins.

Matthews traveled to Germany to receive treatment for an upper-body injury in November 2024 and missed nine games as a result. He then re-aggravated the injury in December and missed a further six games.

Matthews missed Games 5 and 6 of the Leafs’ first-round playoff series against the Bruins in 2024 with what Leafs general manager Brad Treliving later called “head injury issues.”

Not only has 2025-26 been a disappointing season for the Leafs, but Matthews’ injury ends what has been a season full of struggles for him, as well.

Five minutes before suffering the injury, he broke a 12-game goalless drought, the second-longest of his career. Though Matthews has been defensively responsible as a strong two-way forward, he has not come close to the offensive highs he hit earlier in his career. His shot has not looked as powerful, nor has Matthews been as dominant getting to and finishing near the net. Matthews’ 1.11 five-on-five goals per 60 minutes this season ranks as the second-lowest of his career, per Natural Stat Trick — second only to last season.

Matthews captained the United States men’s Olympic team to a gold medal in February. He showcased more offensive firepower in Italy, finishing with three goals and seven points in six games.
